summary: Weekly POC sync focused on planning the rollout/cutover for the Atlas Payments pilot. Key decisions: canary strategy (5% -> 25% ramp), success metrics (p95 latency < 300ms, error rate < 0.5%), monitoring & alerts (golden signals + model quality checks), and runbook ownership. Action items assigned for load testing, runbook drafting, pricing, and compliance docs.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan (AE - Redwood): ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is the weekly pilot sync. we've got a focused agenda today on the rollout and go-live cutover. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Tom (CTO - Atlas): good, thanks. Maya and Arjun are on, Sofia's here for security.
[00:00:18] Maya (Platform Eng): hi all. quick note, we blocked the maintenance window for next friday, tentative from 23:00-01:00 UTC.
[00:00:26] Jordan: perfect, that's helpful. Priya from our SE team will walk through the canary plan and monitoring. Priya?
[00:00:33] Priya (SE - Redwood): yeah hi, um I'll try to keep it granular; apologies for any background noise. so we recommend a phased canary: start at 5% traffic for 1 hour to validate baseline (p50/p95/p99, error rate, model quality checks), then bump to 25% for 2 hours, then 75% for 1 hour before full cutover. if any threshold trips we auto-roll back to previous stable model.
[00:01:00] Arjun (ML Eng - Atlas): can you define the thresholds? like what constitutes a fail?
[00:01:06] Priya: yea. proposed thresholds: p95 latency > 300ms sustained for 5 minutes, or error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes, or model quality drop measured by our eval prompt set dropping below 95% match on intent. also monitor token costs so we don't blow budget during ramp.
[00:01:28] Maya: cost is a big point for us. during the POC we saw some spikes during longer prompts; do you have suggestions for guarding those?
[00:01:36] Priya: yep, recommend prefix caching and request size limits initially. we can enable batch small requests; for long prompts set a higher sampling for dedicated nodes or apply a prompt truncation policy. we can also set a per-route cost guard in the console to block runaway requests. (note: transcription may show KV cash sometimes in notes)
[00:01:56] Sofia (Security): from a compliance angle we need to confirm KMS integration and that audit logs for inference calls are enabled and exported to our SIEM. is that in scope for this pilot?
[00:02:06] Liam (CSM - Redwood): yes, audit logs are supported; Jordan and I will share the doc links. we also support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments for key separation.
[00:02:18] Tom: great. question on network egress — we need to avoid outbound traffic to public endpoints; can Redwood run in our VPC with private peering?
[00:02:25] Priya: yes, Private deployment supports VPC peering and on-prem options. we'll need the network ranges and KMS IAM roles; Maya can provide those.
[00:02:34] Maya: noted, I'll pull the ranges and a list of hostnames.
[00:02:38] Jordan: ok next on the agenda — monitoring & runbooks. Priya, what dashboards should Atlas bake into their SRE console?
[00:02:45] Priya: golden signals: latency (p50/p95/p99), traffic, errors, and saturation of the GPU pool (queue depth, GPU util). also model-quality signals: percent of hallucination flags from the quick eval set, and user-facing fallback rates. we recommend two dashboards: an operations dashboard (latency/errors/capacity) and a quality dashboard (eval metrics, sample outputs). we'll share a Grafana template link.
[00:03:10] Arjun: for model quality checks is there an automated sampling hook to store model outputs for eval? we want to keep PII out of that sampling.
[00:03:17] Priya: yes can enable redaction and sampling at 1% by default; outputs are stored encrypted and can be pushed to your s3 with kms. we can also integrate with your data retention policies.
[00:03:29] Sofia: make sure the retention and redaction settings map to our policy, we can't keep raw outputs longer than 30 days.
[00:03:34] Jordan: copy that. next, rollback strategy — what's the timeline to revert if canary fails?
[00:03:40] Priya: we do fast rollback: if thresholds breach for 5-10 minutes, we switch traffic back to the previous model variant and notify via PagerDuty. rollback is usually under 90s for networked Dedicated deployments, under 3 minutes for hosted depending on cache warming.
[00:03:56] Tom: any risk with in-flight requests during rollback?
[00:04:00] Priya: small window of partial responses — we suggest using idempotency keys client-side and marking partials in logs; we'll surface those in the runbook.
[00:04:08] Maya: on the A/B note, we actually want to run a quality A/B against our heuristics for 48 hours before full cutover. can we split by header so that we can route certain sessions to the canary?
[00:04:18] Priya: yes header-based routing is supported; you can choose percent-based or session-based sticky routing. for quality A/B, sticky by session for 48 hours is best.
[00:04:27] Arjun: what's the recommended canary percentage for ML workloads? 5% is low but may not surface some tail cases.
[00:04:33] Priya: start 5% for sanity checks — we'd suggest moving to 25% within an hour if sanity holds; the 25% window usually shows tail behavior. if you want faster exposure, do a 10% for 2 hours. we wrote these in the pilot runbook.
[00:04:46] Sofia: who owns the runbook? we need clear owners for escalation and approvals.
[00:04:50] Jordan: suggested owners: Atlas ops (Maya) owns Execution, Redwood SE (Priya) owns Rollback and Monitoring configs, Jordan owns commercial decisions, Liam will coordinate the dry-run.
[00:05:00] Tom: ok good. technical deep dive — Priya can you outline the load test profile you'll run?
[00:05:06] Priya: sure — plan: 50 rps steady for 30 minutes at 5% canary, collect p50/p95/p99 and error distribution. then ramp to 200 rps for 10 minutes at 25% for tail. we'll include a few long-prompt sessions mixed in at 5% of traffic to emulate heavy prompts. we'll also run a KV cache warmup to simulate steady state.
[00:05:26] Arjun: will you simulate token distributions? our real workload has many short prompts but a few very long ones.
[00:05:31] Priya: yes, we'll provide a token histogram and replicate your production distribution if you share the sample traces.
[00:05:38] Maya: we'll share sanitized traces after this call.
[00:05:42] Jordan: on the ops side, what alerts should be page-worthy vs ticket-only?
[00:05:47] Priya: page-worthy: error rate > 1% sustained for 1 minute, p99 latency > 1s, or GPU saturation > 90% for 5 minutes. ticket-only: p95 slippage, low-level rate-limited errors. we'll publish recommended thresholds.
[00:06:02] Tom: do you provide SLO templates?
[00:06:05] Liam: yes we have SLO templates and a pricing playbook that maps SLO tiers to Dedicated capacity. Jordan will send pricing options after the call.
[00:06:12] Tom: question on data residency — some EU users need to keep data in EU. can regions be pinned per-route?
[00:06:18] Priya: yes region pinning per-route is supported for Hosted and Dedicated; Private obviously can be deployed in-region. We'll document the region routing policy.
[00:06:27] Sofia: one more security question: do you support SAML SSO for admins and RBAC mapping to our AD groups?
[00:06:33] Jordan: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, plus role-based access controls. we'll share the admin setup guide.
[00:06:41] Maya: ok cool. logistics — timeline for cutover? we are targeting 2026-04-24 for a production cutover pending a successful dry-run.
[00:06:48] Jordan: that gives us about a week. recommended milestones: 1) run load test and canary validation by 4/20, 2) dry-run of runbook between 4/21-4/22, 3) final go/no-go review 4/23, 4) cutover 4/24 during maintenance window.
[00:07:06] Arjun: if the canary shows model-quality regressions, what's the path? do we shadow traffic to the previous model or keep both for A/B?
[00:07:13] Priya: we can do shadowing concurrently to gather more samples without impacting live traffic; but we recommend rolling back if quality fails the threshold. A/B can be used to compare quality metrics side-by-side.
[00:07:23] Tom: any customer references running a similar go-live?
[00:07:26] Jordan: yes we have a payments customer that did a staged rollout using our Dedicated nodes and had a 90s rollback in practice; happy to share a short case study.
[00:07:34] Sofia: let's talk about evidence for compliance — we need to make sure we get the SOC2 report and encryption attestation before signoff.
[00:07:40] Liam: noted — I'll attach our SOC2 Type II and penetration test summary in the follow-up email.
[00:07:46] Maya: can Redwood's observability integrate with our existing Datadog?
[00:07:50] Priya: yes we export metrics and traces to Datadog; logs can be pushed to your ELK or S3. we'll include the integration guide.
[00:07:58] Jordan: ok let's do a quick recap and owners. Priya — run the canary load test and share metrics by 4/20. Jordan — send pricing and runbook template by 4/16. Maya — share sanitized traces and network ranges by 4/18. Sofia — list compliance docs by 4/19. Liam — schedule dry-run by 4/22.
[00:08:20] Tom: thanks everyone. quick note, we may need a one-hour SE on-call during cutover window.
[00:08:27] Priya: happy to be on-call for the cutover dry-run and the cutover itself.
[00:08:31] Jordan: great. any other questions? (short silence) okay we'll follow up with the links. thanks all.
[00:08:42] -- auto-generated summary section possibly imperfect --
[00:09:00] Notes: action items captured above. shared artifacts: Pilot runbook (link: https://redwood.example.com/r/runbook-atlas), Grafana dashboard template (link: https://redwood.example.com/grafana-template), SOC2 and compliance packet (attached in follow-up).
[00:09:20] End of meeting.
